title: Atoms Have Barcodes? Spectra Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Salt falls on a gas flame and it flashes yellow. Fireworks burst red and green. Street lamps glow orange. Every element glows in its own colours, like a barcode. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 2, Structure of Atom) we read the hydrogen spectrum line by line.

You will see white light spread into a continuous spectrum, a glowing gas give only a few bright lines (emission spectrum), and cool gas take the same lines out of white light (absorption spectrum). On the molecule bench, a hydrogen electron jumps up, falls back and sends out one photon, and each fall to orbit 2 lights one Balmer line: about 656 nm (red), 486, 434 and 410 nm. Falls to orbit 1 give the Lyman series (ultraviolet), and falls to orbits 3, 4 and 5 give the Paschen, Brackett and Pfund series (infrared). We build the Rydberg formula step by step, work out the wavelength of the red line (656.5 nm), then the exam trap about n1 and n2, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 16 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.
